summary: A scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Caumanns earned his MA at the University of Hamburg under David P. Jackson and his PhD at the University of Munich under Franz-Karl Ehrhard, later holding posts at Munich, Lumbini, and Bern.

Grabowsky works in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Kiel, Chiang Mai, and Hamburg, he held posts at Passau, Laos, Münster, and Hamburg, where he became chair of Thai language and culture in 2009.

Specializing in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies, Zotz studied at the University of Vienna and under Anagarika Govinda. His career includes academic posts at Vienna, Otani, Ryukoku, Saarland University, and the University of Luxembourg.

A scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy who taught Mark S. G. Dyczkowski, Dvivedi served as head of the Yogatantra Department at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and as Deputy Director of the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies.
Working in the field of Buddhist studies, Jayasuriya studied under Rerukane Ariyaratne, H. D. Dharmasiriwardhana, and M. U. Sri Kaveeswara.

A scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies, Rouse studied at Regent's Park College, Christ's College, and Cambridge. He was a Fellow at Christ's College and held teaching posts at Bedford, Cheltenham, Rugby, and The Perse School.

Rivers studied medicine at the University of London and St Bartholomew's. Active in history, archaeology, and psychology, he held medical posts, taught at Cambridge, and became a Fellow at St John's College and president of the Anthropological Society.

Brown, who worked in Indology, linguistics, and history/archaeology, studied at Johns Hopkins under Maurice Bloomfield and Franklin Edgerton. He held posts at Johns Hopkins and Government Sri Pratap Memorial Rajput College, and was a longtime professor at Pennsylvania.

Working in religious studies, Indology, and Buddhist studies, Kloetzli earned his PhD at the University of Chicago, studying under teachers including Mircea Eliade and Paul Tillich. He taught at American University, George Washington University, and Dartmouth College.

A scholar of linguistics, Buddhist studies, and Indology, Karunatillake served as a professor at the University of Kelaniya and was a Visiting Numata Professor of Buddhist Studies at Harvard University in 1998.

Specializing in religious studies, sinology, and Buddhist studies, Tam earned his PhD at McMaster University under Koichi Shinohara. He became a professor and department chairperson at The Chinese University of Hong Kong.

Rahula studied at Ceylon, Calcutta, and the Sorbonne under Paul Demiéville. Active in Buddhist studies and Indology, he was a professor at Northwestern University and Vice-Chancellor of the University of Sri Jayewardenepura, with posts at Oxford, Swarthmore, and UCLA.

Henning was an Iranian, Central Asian, and linguistics scholar who studied at the University of Göttingen. He held academic posts at SOAS and the University of London, Columbia University, and the University of California, Berkeley.

Working in history, archaeology, Indology, and linguistics, Elliot was educated at East India Company College and the College of Fort St George. From 1837 to 1842, he served as Private Secretary to Lord Elphinstone in the Madras Government.

Clark, a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies, earned his degrees at Harvard and studied under Richard Pischel. He served as Instructor in Sanskrit at Chicago before becoming Harvard's Wales Professor of Sanskrit from 1927 to 1950.

Specializing in sinology, Buddhist studies, and Indology, Liebenthal earned his doctorate at Breslau. He held appointments at the Sino-Indian Institute, Peking University, Visva-Bharati University, Hebrew University of Jerusalem, the Sorbonne, and the University of Tübingen.

Spink, who worked in history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies, studied at Amherst College and Harvard University. He taught at Brandeis University from 1956 to 1961 and served as a professor at the University of Michigan from ~1961 to 2000.
Working in Buddhist studies, Nowick studied at the Juilliard School and under Zuigan Goto in Japan from 1950 to 1965. He held a post at Kyoto Women's University and founded Moonspring Hermitage.
Piston studied at the Massachusetts College of Art and Design and Harvard University. He held an academic post at Harvard University from approximately 1926 to 1960.

A scholar in linguistics and Indology, Porzig studied at the University of Jena and under Wilhelm Streitberg. He held academic posts at the universities of Leipzig, Bern, Jena, and Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz.
